about.title: Santa Monica Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Monica packs a lot of traffic into a small footprint. Beach visitors funnel down Lincoln Boulevard, commuters pour off the I-10 where the Santa Monica Freeway ends, and Pacific Coast Highway carries a steady stream north out of town. In 2025, the city recorded 445 injury collisions, with 572 people injured and 5 lives lost. Public records show reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m., when the workweek and the weekend crowd overlap. If you were hurt in one of those collisions, the days that follow can feel disorienting: medical appointments, calls from an adjuster you did not choose, and a car you may not be able to drive. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are a free service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened, and we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Los Angeles County and works on contingency. You decide whether to move forward; there is no charge for the introduction.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Monica Drivers Start With LawProactive

items.title: The clock is already running
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident injury claims, but if a city, county, or state vehicle or road condition was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting connected early protects those deadlines.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame; your share of responsibility simply reduces the amount. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Evidence and recorded statements matter
items.desc: Dashcam footage, 4th Street business cameras, and witness contacts fade fast, and the other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement before you have counsel. The attorneys in our network help you preserve what matters and speak on your behalf.

items.question: My crash happened on Pacific Coast Highway. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can. PCH is a state route, so if a road condition, signal, or public vehicle played a role, part of your claim may be against a government entity, and that generally requires a formal claim within six months rather than the usual two years. An attorney can sort out who is potentially responsible and which deadlines apply before anything lapses.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to assign you more fault later under California's comparative fault system. You can simply tell them your attorney will be in touch.

items.question: How does LawProactive get paid if the service is free?
items.answer: You never pay LawProactive anything. The independent attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, which means their fee comes out of any recovery they obtain for you, and if there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee. Whether to hire the attorney is entirely your choice.
